hook.text: In 2016, a smart contract called The DAO raised $150 million, then a bug let a hacker drain $60 million.

buildup.text: Smart contracts are programs on a blockchain. They execute automatically when conditions are met. No middleman needed.

discovery.text: Example: insurance that auto-pays if a flight is delayed. The contract checks data and sends money. No claims process.

twist.text: Code is law—but code has bugs. Unlike paper contracts, you can't argue intent. The program does exactly what it says.

climax.text: Smart contracts could automate huge parts of finance and law. But trusting code means trusting the programmers.

punchline.text: Automatic agreements. No humans. No excuses.

quiz.question: What is a smart contract?
options: A self-executing program on a blockchain
